extracted.intended_audience: critical readers, literary critics, and aspiring novelists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reading, evaluating, and reconstructing the form of a novel: how a critic should treat the material, detect forms and faults, and recreate the book as a coherent artistic object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recreate the novel as a single, welded mass
rubrics_metrics.description: “The tale is complete, and the book stands before us, or should stand, as a welded mass.” The reader must fashion the many fragments and impressions into a compact fabric — a single form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately marshal and concentrate the procession of reading into a coherent object; acknowledge memory failures but aim to perceive the volume as an imposing, appraisable object representing the author's intention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader as co-creator / novelist
rubrics_metrics.description: “The reader of a novel ... is himself a novelist; he is the maker of a book which may or may not please his taste when it is finished.” The critic must take responsibility for constructing the book in his mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be a passive receptor; actively recreate the book's form and accept responsibility for the result while recognizing the difference in powers between author and critic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain critical distance from material
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is an effort ... to keep the world of Anna ... at a distance; and yet it must be kept at a distance if it is to be impressed with the form of art.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stand above the material rather than being swept by it so you can perceive design and form; avoid being beset or swayed by the immediacy of the depicted life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build impressions into a structure in a workmanlike manner
rubrics_metrics.description: “The impressions that succeed one another ... are to be built into a structure, and the critic is missing his opportunity unless he can proceed in a workmanlike manner.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the reader's task as craftsmanship: recognize components, arrange impressions consciously, and assemble them into coherent shape rather than relying on mere appreciation of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know and recognize the various forms/substances of narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: “They are the various forms of narrative, the forms in which a story may be told ... to use them is easier than to perceive their demands and their qualities.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn to identify narrative types (scenic, dramatic, pictorial, generalized, etc.), their demands and qualities, by reading critically and observing how scenes and figures are presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine methods of successful novelists and notice their devices
rubrics_metrics.description: “Let us very carefully follow the methods of the novelists whose effects are incontestable, noticing exactly the manner in which the scenes and figures in their books are presented.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study episodes to see what arts and devices produce relief, vividness, and intelligibility (how an episode is given relief, how a character is made vivid), and transfer those observations into critical judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and use precise critical vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.description: The essay laments “the singular poverty of our critical vocabulary” and the uncertain technical acceptation of terms like 'dramatic', 'pictorial', 'scenic' or 'generalized' narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulate and adopt clear definitions for critical terms so discussion of novel structure can be exact; avoid relying on vague, unrounded phrases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have the analytical courage to dissect a novel
rubrics_metrics.description: “We still suffer from a kind of shyness in the presence of a novel ... It spoils the fun of a novel to know how it is made — is this a reflection that lurks at the back of our minds?”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be deterred by the illusion of life; analyse the form without romantic scruple — the pleasure of creating (reconstructing the form) outweighs preserving the illusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge whether an author's proceeding is right for the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: “Is this proceeding of the author the right one, the best for the subject? Is it possible to conceive and to name a better?”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate authorial choices (sequence, emphasis, digression) by asking whether they serve the subject; when treatment diverges or contradicts the subject, locate and assess those turns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess the form's completeness and its relation to the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: “If the form is to the eye imperfect, it means that the subject is somehow and somewhere imperfectly expressed ... Where then, and how?”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the finished book seems flawed, investigate whether the fault lies in starting from the wrong center, divergence in development, or a poor/unfruitful subject; trace the ramification of the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect competing themes or incoherent unification
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic should notice when a work contains two large, conflicting motives (e.g., Tolstoy writing both the universal cycle of youth/age and a national saga of war) that are not unified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace exact places where the centre shifts, mark thematic cleavages, and assess whether juxtaposed themes merge, contrast, or merely interrupt one another; lack of unity is a legitimate ground for criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect the novelist's selection and arrangement before criticising
rubrics_metrics.description: “There can be no picking and choosing now; that was the business of the novelist, and it has been accomplished according to his light; the critic creates out of life that is already subject to art.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that the critic must work with the material already selected and arranged by the author; criticism is reconstruction from material already shaped by artistic choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and treat (or ignore) authorial exposition/pamphleteering as distinct from fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Tolstoy sometimes abandons fiction to ‘chapters of comment and explanation, chapters in the manner of a controversial pamphlet.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish dramatic/narrative material from didactic or argumentative digressions; these may be judged separately or, where irrelevant, skimmed or skipped in forming an overall judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine whether historical/episodic material functions as central theme or background
rubrics_metrics.description: When historical scenes (war, political events) recur, decide if they are episodic background or intended as the book's organising motive (e.g., whether 'war' or 'the cycle of youth' is the true subject).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze how public/historic events relate to personal narratives: are they used to illuminate the universal theme or do they assert a separate, competing centre? This distinction affects judgments of unity and appropriateness of scale.
